tali cohortatione militum facta classis ab utrisque in proelium deducitur: the ablative absolute closes the briefing in a few words and the historic present deducitur moves both fleets out at once, quickening the pace
quarum acie constituta, priusquam signum pugnae daretur: the clauses hold the fighting back at the very moment it should begin, keeping the reader waiting
Hannibal, ut palam faceret suis, quo loco Eumenes esset: the sentence breaks off on the purpose of Hannibal’s move, so the reader knows what he intends but must wait to see how he does it

essays.q: how does Nepos make Hannibal’s trick with the messenger entertaining for the reader?
points: the trick takes place in the tense moment before the signal for battle
the reader is told the messenger’s real purpose before the enemy can guess it
the messenger looks harmless and official, with a small boat and a herald’s staff
the enemy assume the letter is about peace and take him straight to the king
his real task, pointing out the king’s ship, is done almost in passing, and he returns safely
the letter contains nothing but mockery, so Eumenes is humiliated before the battle
Eumenes is baffled yet joins battle at once, while the reader knows he is heading into a trap
features: priusquam signum pugnae daretur: the temporal clause sets the trick in the tense pause before battle, which makes the episode a lively interlude
Hannibal, ut palam faceret suis, quo loco Eumenes esset: the reader is told the real purpose of the messenger in advance, so we enjoy watching the enemy fall for the trick

tabellarium in scapha cum caduceo mittit: the tiny boat and the herald’s staff make the messenger look harmless and official, an amusing disguise for a spy, and the crisp historic present mittit shows Hannibal acting at once
epistulamque ostendens se regem professus est quaerere: the letter held up for all to see is the bait, and the messenger’s bold claim to be looking for the king is comic in its cheek

statim ad Eumenem deductus est, quod nemo dubitabat, quin aliquid de pace esset scriptum: statim and the sweeping nemo dubitabat show the whole enemy fleet confidently wrong, which is ironic and entertaining

tabellarius ducis nave declarata suis eodem, unde erat egressus, se recepit: the real purpose of the mission is achieved almost in passing in an ablative absolute, and the messenger slips back where he came from as if nothing had happened
at Eumenes soluta epistula nihil in ea repperit, nisi quae ad irridendum eum pertinerent: at marks the turn to the victim, and nihil … nisi reveals the joke: the letter contains nothing but mockery
cuius etsi causam mirabatur neque reperiebat: the pair of verbs shows Eumenes baffled and puzzling, while the reader is in on the secret
tamen proelium statim committere non dubitavit: the litotes makes Eumenes seem bold, which is amusing because the reader knows he is rushing into the trap

essays.q: how does Nepos contrast Hannibal and Eumenes?
points: Hannibal is in control from the start, acting before the signal for battle
he uses a messenger with a herald’s staff to find out where Eumenes is
Eumenes’ side is easily fooled, sure that the letter is about peace
the messenger returns safely with his mission done
Hannibal mocks Eumenes with an insulting letter
Eumenes is baffled and cannot find the reason
he joins battle at once, into the trap Hannibal has set
features: Hannibal, ut palam faceret suis, quo loco Eumenes esset: Hannibal’s name stands at the centre of the long sentence, and the purpose clause shows him thinking ahead, in contrast with an enemy who suspects nothing
tabellarium in scapha cum caduceo mittit: the historic present mittit shows Hannibal acting decisively, using the sacred herald’s staff with calculated cunning

statim ad Eumenem deductus est, quod nemo dubitabat, quin aliquid de pace esset scriptum: Eumenes’ side is shown credulous: nemo dubitabat stresses that not one of them suspects a trick, while Hannibal has planned it all
tabellarius ducis nave declarata suis eodem, unde erat egressus, se recepit: the ablative absolute shows Hannibal’s plan succeeding with effortless ease, as his man returns unharmed

at Eumenes soluta epistula nihil in ea repperit, nisi quae ad irridendum eum pertinerent: at sharply turns from Hannibal’s success to Eumenes’ humiliation, and nihil … nisi shows Hannibal’s contempt for the king
cuius etsi causam mirabatur neque reperiebat: the two verbs show Eumenes confused and unable to understand, the opposite of the clear-sighted Hannibal
tamen proelium statim committere non dubitavit: the litotes and statim show Eumenes acting rashly without thought, in contrast with Hannibal’s careful planning

essays.lemma: qui ubi ad naves … fuga salutem petiit
essays.q: how does Nepos make Eumenes look foolish?
points: his side lets an enemy messenger through and takes him straight to the king
everyone assumes the letter must be about peace
the messenger openly gives away the king’s ship to his own side
the letter contains nothing but mockery
Eumenes is puzzled and cannot work out what it means
he still joins battle at once without hesitation
the whole Bithynian fleet attacks his ship and the king has to flee for his life
features: epistulamque ostendens se regem professus est quaerere, statim ad Eumenem deductus est: Eumenes’ men take an enemy messenger straight to their king, and statim stresses how easily they are fooled
quod nemo dubitabat, quin aliquid de pace esset scriptum: the sweeping nemo dubitabat shows the whole of Eumenes’ side confidently wrong, which makes them look naive

tabellarius ducis nave declarata suis eodem, unde erat egressus, se recepit: the ablative absolute shows the king’s ship given away almost in passing, and the messenger leaves unhindered, as if Eumenes’ side noticed nothing

at Eumenes soluta epistula nihil in ea repperit, nisi quae ad irridendum eum pertinerent: at turns to the king himself, and nihil … nisi reveals that the letter he has been waiting for is pure mockery: he is the butt of the joke
cuius etsi causam mirabatur neque reperiebat: the pair of verbs shows Eumenes puzzling and failing to see what the reader sees at once
tamen proelium statim committere non dubitavit: tamen and the litotes show him rushing into battle in spite of his confusion, which makes his boldness look foolish

horum in concursu Bithynii Hannibalis praecepto universi navem Eumenis adoriuntur: universi and the historic present adoriuntur show the whole enemy fleet bearing down on his ship, exactly as the trick intended
quorum vim rex cum sustinere non posset, fuga salutem petiit: rex is set against fuga: the king who rushed into battle is reduced to running for his life

essays.q: how does Nepos make the defeat of the Pergamene fleet dramatic?
points: the king himself cannot withstand the attack and only just escapes to his defences on the shore
the rest of the Pergamene fleet is winning, which makes the sudden reversal more striking
Nepos reminds the reader of the pots, so the reader knows their secret when the Pergamenes do not
the Pergamenes first laugh at the pots, and the laughter turns to terror
the shock of the snakes and the sailors’ confusion about which danger to avoid
their flight back to camp completes the rout
Nepos ends by praising Hannibal’s strategy, which he says often won him battles on land as well
features: quorum vim rex cum sustinere non posset, fuga salutem petiit: the contrast of vim with fuga shows the king himself overwhelmed and forced to flee at the start of the account
quam consecutus non esset, nisi intra sua praesidia se recepisset: the past unreal condition shows how narrow his escape was, which heightens the drama
reliquae Pergamenae naves cum adversarios premerent acrius: the comparative acrius shows the rest of the Pergamene fleet winning, so the sudden reversal that follows is all the more dramatic

repente in eas vasa fictilia, de quibus supra mentionem fecimus, conici coepta sunt: repente comes first for surprise, and the narrator’s aside reminds the reader what is in the pots, creating dramatic irony
quae iacta initio risum pugnantibus concitarunt: the Pergamenes laugh at the clay pots, and initio warns that the mood is about to change
postquam autem naves suas oppletas conspexerunt serpentibus: serpentibus is held back to the end of the clause, so the snakes arrive as a shock, just as they did for the sailors

nova re perterriti, cum, quid potissimum vitarent, non viderent: the intensifying prefix of perterriti and the indirect question convey panic and confusion as the sailors cannot tell which danger to avoid
puppes verterunt seque ad sua castra nautica rettulerunt: the vivid image of turning the sterns, followed by the second verb, shows the rout completed in a few swift words
sic Hannibal consilio arma Pergamenorum superavit: the juxtaposition of consilio and arma sums up the drama as brains defeating force, with Hannibal’s name placed in the climactic final sentence

essays.q: how does Nepos show that Hannibal’s plan worked exactly as he intended?
points: the Bithynians attack Eumenes’ ship all together, just as Hannibal ordered
the king cannot withstand them and flees
he only just escapes to his defences on the shore
the rest of the Pergamene fleet seems to be winning until the pots arrive
the pots are thrown, and at first the enemy laughs
when the snakes appear the Pergamenes panic at the unheard-of attack
unable to decide which danger to avoid, they turn and flee to their camp
features: horum in concursu Bithynii Hannibalis praecepto universi navem Eumenis adoriuntur: Hannibalis praecepto and universi show the Bithynians carrying out his order to the letter, every ship attacking the king’s
quorum vim rex cum sustinere non posset, fuga salutem petiit: the king cannot withstand the combined assault, just as Hannibal’s plan to target one ship intended
quam consecutus non esset, nisi intra sua praesidia se recepisset: the past unreal condition shows how close the plan came to capturing the king
reliquae Pergamenae naves cum adversarios premerent acrius: the rest of the enemy fleet is winning, which shows that the snakes were needed and that Hannibal had foreseen it

repente in eas vasa fictilia, de quibus supra mentionem fecimus, conici coepta sunt: the narrator’s aside links the pots back to Hannibal’s preparations, so the reader sees the second stage of the plan unfold as designed
quae iacta initio risum pugnantibus concitarunt, neque, quare id fieret, poterat intellegi: the enemy laugh and cannot understand, which shows that the trick stays hidden until it works
postquam autem naves suas oppletas conspexerunt serpentibus, nova re perterriti: the delayed serpentibus and perterriti show the snakes having exactly the terrifying effect Hannibal intended

cum, quid potissimum vitarent, non viderent, puppes verterunt seque ad sua castra nautica rettulerunt: the indirect question shows total confusion, and the two verbs of flight complete the rout Hannibal had planned

essays.q: how does Nepos use this episode to confirm his view of Hannibal as a great general?
points: King Eumenes is reduced to running away
Hannibal’s planning reverses the battle just when the Pergamenes seem to be winning
the enemy is beaten by a weapon nobody could have prepared for
the panic of the Pergamenes shows how completely they are outwitted
Nepos sums up the victory as strategy defeating armed force
he widens it into proof that Hannibal often won on land too
he credits the victories to Hannibal’s skill and good judgement
features: quorum vim rex cum sustinere non posset, fuga salutem petiit: the contrast of vim and fuga shows Rome’s ally reduced to flight by Hannibal’s plan

reliquae Pergamenae naves cum adversarios premerent acrius, repente in eas vasa fictilia … conici coepta sunt: repente marks the moment Hannibal’s planning reverses a battle the enemy seemed to be winning
quae iacta initio risum pugnantibus concitarunt, neque, quare id fieret, poterat intellegi: the enemy’s laughter and their failure to understand show how far ahead of them Hannibal’s thinking is
nova re perterriti, cum, quid potissimum vitarent, non viderent: nova stresses that no one had met such a weapon before, which marks the originality of Hannibal as a general
puppes verterunt seque ad sua castra nautica rettulerunt: the swift account of the enemy’s flight shows how complete the victory is
sic Hannibal consilio arma Pergamenorum superavit: sic draws the conclusion, and the juxtaposition of consilio and arma sums up Nepos’ view that Hannibal wins by intelligence
neque tum solum, sed saepe alias pedestribus copiis: the general statement widens one episode into proof of a whole career, on land as well as at sea
pari prudentia pepulit adversarios: prudentia names the quality Nepos most admires in Hannibal, so the Life’s account of his generalship closes on a confirmed judgement

essays.q: how does Nepos build up a sense of danger around Hannibal?
points: Flamininus wastes no time and reports the news the next day
the senate thinks Rome will never be free of plots while Hannibal is alive, which shows how much he is still feared
an embassy including Flamininus is sent to demand that Hannibal be handed over
Prusias does not dare to refuse
he hides behind the law of hospitality while telling the Romans they can find Hannibal easily
Hannibal has prepared for this moment by building exits on every side of his house
Nepos tells the reader that what Hannibal feared did in fact happen, creating suspense
features: id postero die Flamininus senatui detulit: the precise time phrase postero die shows the news acted on at once, so the threat to Hannibal gathers speed

qui Hannibale vivo numquam se sine insidiis futuros existimarent: the ablative absolute Hannibale vivo and the double negative numquam … sine show how deeply the senate still fears him, which marks him out for death
ne inimicissimum suum secum haberet sibique dederet: the superlative inimicissimum shows how bitter the Roman hostility is, and the demand to hand him over makes the danger direct
his Prusias negare ausus non est: the litotes shows his protector too afraid of Rome to refuse, so Hannibal is left without defence
illud recusavit, ne id a se fieri postularent, quod adversus ius hospitii esset: Prusias hides behind the law of hospitality, a hollow protection that leaves Hannibal exposed
ipsi, si possent, comprehenderent; locum ubi esset, facile inventuros: the curt reported commands and facile show how easily Hannibal can be found, which makes the danger feel close
Hannibal enim uno loco se tenebat, in castello: uno loco shows Hannibal staying in one place, a fixed target for his enemies
idque sic aedificarat, ut in omnibus partibus aedificii exitus haberet: the result clause shows that Hannibal himself has long expected an attack, which adds to the sense of threat
scilicet verens, ne usu veniret, quod accidit: the clause of fearing and the blunt quod accidit tell the reader that the feared moment has come, leaving the passage on a note of foreboding

essays.q: how does Nepos make Hannibal’s last moments dramatic?
points: the house is surrounded by a large force of armed men
the scene is seen through the eyes of a boy at the door, which makes it small and personal
Hannibal stays calm and practical, sending the boy round every door
the exits he built so carefully are all blocked
he sees at once that he is being hunted and that this is no accident
he chooses to die by his own hand rather than at the will of his enemies
he acts in keeping with his past courage, and the narrative ends on his taking the poison
features: huc cum legati Romanorum venissent ac multitudine domum eius circumdedissent: the house surrounded by a great number of men sets the scene of a trap closing in on its victim

puer ab ianua prospiciens Hannibali dixit plures praeter consuetudinem armatos apparere: the scene is seen through the eyes of a boy at the door, and praeter consuetudinem signals that something is badly wrong, which builds tension
ut omnes fores aedificii circumiret ac propere sibi nuntiaret, num eodem modo undique obsideretur: Hannibal’s urgent orders (propere) and the indirect question keep the reader waiting for the answer
puer cum celeriter, quid esset, renuntiasset omnesque exitus occupatos ostendisset: celeriter quickens the pace, and omnes exitus occupatos reveals that every escape route is cut off
sensit id non fortuito factum, sed se peti: the antithesis marks the moment of realisation: Hannibal understands that he is being hunted
neque sibi diutius vitam esse retinendam: the gerundive presents his decision to die as reached at once, which makes the moment stark
quam ne alieno arbitrio dimitteret, memor pristinarum virtutum: the purpose clause and memor show him choosing his death to keep control, a dignified and moving climax
venenum, quod semper secum habere consuerat, sumpsit: semper reveals the poison he has carried all along, and sumpsit is held to the very end, so the scene closes on his final act

essays.lemma: quae dum in Asia … facile inventuros
essays.q: how does Nepos present the Romans and Prusias in their dealings over Hannibal?
points: the Romans learn where Hannibal is by chance, at a dinner party
Flamininus reports it to the senate the very next day
the senate fears it will never be free of plots while Hannibal lives
they send envoys, Flamininus among them, to demand that Prusias hand him over
they call Hannibal their bitterest enemy
Prusias does not dare to refuse
he hides behind the laws of hospitality while telling the Romans where to find him
features: quae dum in Asia geruntur, accidit casu: accidit casu presents Hannibal’s betrayal as beginning by mere chance, which makes the Romans’ discovery seem casual
ut legati Prusiae Romae apud T. Quinctium Flamininum consularem cenarent: Prusias’ own envoys are dining with a Roman former consul, which shows Prusias’ court on friendly terms with Rome

atque ibi de Hannibale mentione facta ex his unus diceret eum in Prusiae regno esse: the ablative absolute makes the mention of Hannibal offhand: Prusias’ envoy gives away his master’s guest in idle talk
id postero die Flamininus senatui detulit: postero die shows the Romans acting at once on the information
qui Hannibale vivo numquam se sine insidiis futuros existimarent: Hannibale vivo and numquam … sine present the senators as still afraid of one old man
ne inimicissimum suum secum haberet sibique dederet: the superlative inimicissimum and the blunt demand present the Romans as relentless in their hatred
his Prusias negare ausus non est: the litotes presents Prusias as too afraid of Rome to refuse
illud recusavit, ne id a se fieri postularent, quod adversus ius hospitii esset: Prusias keeps to the letter of hospitality, which makes his betrayal look hypocritical

ipsi, si possent, comprehenderent; locum ubi esset, facile inventuros: the curt reported commands show Prusias in effect telling the Romans where to find Hannibal, and facile shows how little protection he offers

essays.q: how does Nepos present Hannibal as calm and in control at the end of his life?
points: he had foreseen the danger and built his fortress with exits on every side
when the boy reports armed men, he gives clear, practical orders
he checks whether he is surrounded on all sides
he grasps the situation at once: the Romans are hunting him
he decides calmly that he should not keep his life
he chooses to die on his own terms, at no one else’s will
mindful of his past courage, he takes the poison he always carried
features: idque sic aedificarat, ut in omnibus partibus aedificii exitus haberet: the result clause shows Hannibal’s foresight: he has planned for this danger in the very design of his house
scilicet verens, ne usu veniret, quod accidit: his fear is presented as clear-sighted planning, and quod accidit shows that he judged the danger correctly
qui imperavit ei, ut omnes fores aedificii circumiret ac propere sibi nuntiaret: the clear command (imperavit) shows him giving orders like a general even in his own house
num eodem modo undique obsideretur: the calm, practical indirect question shows him assessing his position before he acts
sensit id non fortuito factum, sed se peti: the antithesis shows him grasping the truth at once and without panic
neque sibi diutius vitam esse retinendam: the gerundive presents his death as a conclusion he reaches calmly
quam ne alieno arbitrio dimitteret: the purpose clause shows him keeping control of his fate, refusing to die at another’s will
memor pristinarum virtutum: memor shows him mindful of his past courage, so his death is a deliberate act worthy of his life
venenum, quod semper secum habere consuerat, sumpsit: semper shows that he had prepared even for this, and the final verb sumpsit ends on his own decisive action

essays.lemma: puer cum celeriter … M. Baebio Tamphilo
essays.q: how does Nepos bring the Life of Hannibal to a fitting close?
points: Hannibal understands his position at once and reaches his decision calmly
he keeps control by choosing the manner of his own death
his suicide is presented as worthy of his past courage, a noble death
the poison he always kept with him shows his foresight to the very end
Nepos gives a final verdict of the highest praise, ‘the bravest of men’
his death is described gently as a rest after a life of many hardships
Nepos ends as a careful scholar, setting out the different dates his sources give
features: sensit id non fortuito factum, sed se peti: the antithesis shows Hannibal seeing the truth at once, so he faces death with the clear judgement shown throughout the Life
quam ne alieno arbitrio dimitteret, memor pristinarum virtutum: the purpose clause and memor present his suicide as a noble death in keeping with his past courage, a fitting end to his story
venenum, quod semper secum habere consuerat, sumpsit: semper shows his lifelong foresight, and sumpsit held to the end closes the narrative on his own final act
sic vir fortissimus: sic draws the story together, and the superlative fortissimus gives a final verdict of the highest praise, which echoes the admiration with which the Life began
multis variisque perfunctus laboribus: the pair of adjectives sums up the long and eventful life told in the previous chapters
anno acquievit septuagesimo: the gentle verb acquievit presents death as rest after hardship, and the hyperbaton leaves his great age as the final word of the narrative
quibus consulibus interierit, non convenit: the abrupt change of tone moves from the story to the scholar, closing the Life with a historian’s care

namque Atticus … at Polybius … Sulpicius autem Blitho: the tricolon of authorities, each introduced by a new connective, shows Nepos weighing his sources and leaving the question open, an honest ending for a biography

essays.lemma: huc cum legati … anno acquievit septuagesimo
essays.q: how does Nepos make Hannibal’s death moving?
points: the great general is trapped in his own house by Roman envoys
the danger is reported by a boy at the door
his careful precautions fail: every exit is blocked
he realises that he is being hunted
he chooses death to keep control of his fate, mindful of his past courage
he takes the poison he had always kept with him
Nepos’ final verdict calls him the bravest of men, who found rest after many hardships
features: huc cum legati Romanorum venissent ac multitudine domum eius circumdedissent: the great general is trapped in his own house by a crowd of men, a pitiful reversal for Rome’s great enemy
puer ab ianua prospiciens Hannibali dixit plures praeter consuetudinem armatos apparere: the danger is reported by a boy at the door, which makes Hannibal’s last moments small, personal and touching
omnesque exitus occupatos ostendisset: the exits he built with such care are all blocked, so his precautions fail at the last
sensit id non fortuito factum, sed se peti: the antithesis marks the painful moment when he realises that he is being hunted
neque sibi diutius vitam esse retinendam: the gerundive shows him accepting quietly that his life must end, which makes the moment more moving
quam ne alieno arbitrio dimitteret, memor pristinarum virtutum: he dies on his own terms, remembering his past courage, which gives his death dignity
venenum, quod semper secum habere consuerat, sumpsit: the detail that he had always carried poison suggests a life lived in constant danger, and sumpsit closes on his last act

sic vir fortissimus, multis variisque perfunctus laboribus, anno acquievit septuagesimo: the superlative fortissimus, the pair multis variisque and the gentle verb acquievit present his death as a well-earned rest after a life of hardship, a moving final tribute
